definition: A cloud benefit where businesses shift from large upfront capital expenditures on hardware to variable operational expenditures, paying only for what they consume.

A financial estimate that includes the full cost of an IT investment over its lifetime, covering hardware, software, operations, and maintenance. Cloud TCO comparisons typically show savings versus on-premises.
The ability to automatically scale compute resources up or down in response to demand, ensuring capacity matches usage at any given time without manual intervention.
The cost advantage AWS achieves by operating at massive scale, which allows it to offer lower pay-as-you-go prices than customers could achieve by operating their own infrastructure.
The practice of selecting the smallest AWS resource type that meets workload requirements, avoiding over-provisioning and reducing cost without degrading performance.
A system design goal that ensures an application remains operational during failures by deploying redundant resources across multiple Availability Zones so no single failure causes an outage.
An AWS cloud benefit that allows companies to deploy applications in multiple geographic regions worldwide in a short time, enabling low-latency access for global users.
A cloud characteristic that allows users to provision and manage computing resources independently through a console or API without requiring human interaction with the cloud provider.
Physically separate data centers within an AWS Region, each with independent power, networking, and cooling. Deploying across multiple AZs provides fault isolation and high availability.
An AWS pricing model where customers pay only for the resources they consume, with no upfront commitments or termination fees, enabling cost alignment with actual usage.
One of the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focused on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value, and continually improving processes and procedures.
One of the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focused on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads through efficient resource use and reducing carbon footprint.
An AWS best practice of architecting systems to assume components will fail, using redundancy, retries, and failover mechanisms so failures are automatically handled without service disruption.

An architectural pattern where components interact through well-defined interfaces (such as queues or APIs) and are minimally dependent on each other, so failures in one component do not cascade to others.
An AWS service that helps review workloads against best practices across the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework, providing a prioritized list of improvements.

A framework that divides security responsibilities between AWS and the customer. AWS is responsible for security 'of' the cloud (infrastructure), while customers are responsible for security 'in' the cloud (data, applications, access).
A portal that provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and agreements, such as SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and Business Associate Agreements (BAA).
A managed service for creating and controlling encryption keys used to protect data at rest and in transit across AWS services and customer applications.
A service that continuously monitors and records AWS resource configurations, evaluates them against desired compliance rules, and provides configuration history for auditing and change management.
A managed threat detection service that continuously analyzes CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs using machine learning to identify suspicious activity and potential threats.
A cloud security posture management service that aggregates security findings from AWS services and third-party tools into a centralized dashboard with prioritized remediation guidance.
A managed DDoS protection service that provides always-on detection, automatic mitigation, access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT), and financial protections against DDoS-related cost spikes.
Automatic DDoS protection included at no cost for all AWS customers, defending against common network and transport layer attacks for services like CloudFront, Route 53, and ELB.

A mechanism that allows users to authenticate with an external identity provider (like Active Directory or Google) and receive temporary AWS credentials, enabling single sign-on without creating individual IAM users.

term: AWS managed policies vs customer-managed IAM policies
definition: AWS managed policies are pre-built by AWS for common use cases and updated automatically; customer-managed policies are created and controlled by the account owner for fine-grained, custom permissions.
A service that issues temporary security credentials for IAM roles and identity federation. Temporary credentials expire automatically, reducing the risk of credential exposure.
A service for adding user authentication, authorization, and user management to web and mobile apps. Provides user pools for identity management and identity pools for temporary AWS access.

An IAM tool that analyzes resource-based policies to identify resources (S3 buckets, KMS keys, IAM roles, etc.) that are accessible from outside the account, helping detect unintended public or cross-account access.
An automated vulnerability management service that continuously scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure, providing risk scores.

A security management service that allows administrators to centrally configure and enforce AWS WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections, and security groups across multiple accounts and resources in an AWS Organization.
A cloud-based hardware security module (HSM) that provides dedicated physical hardware for generating and storing cryptographic keys, meeting the strictest compliance requirements for key storage.
A service that provisions, manages, and renews SSL/TLS certificates for use with AWS services such as ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway, with automatic renewal at no additional cost.
An advanced IAM feature that sets the maximum permissions an IAM entity (user or role) can have, regardless of what their identity-based policies grant. Used to limit privilege escalation.
A fully managed Microsoft Active Directory in the AWS Cloud that supports AD-dependent workloads and applications, with MFA support and trust relationships with on-premises AD.
A managed stateful network firewall and intrusion prevention service for VPCs that provides fine-grained control over traffic with domain-based filtering, IPS rules, and TLS inspection.
An infrastructure-as-code service that allows you to define AWS resources in JSON or YAML templates and provision them in a repeatable, automated, and version-controlled way.

An open-source framework that allows developers to define AWS infrastructure using familiar programming languages such as Python, TypeScript, or Java, which are synthesized into CloudFormation templates.
A serverless workflow orchestration service that coordinates the execution of multiple AWS services into structured workflows using visual state machines, with built-in error handling and retries.
A Systems Manager capability that allows remote execution of commands or scripts on EC2 instances and on-premises servers at scale without requiring SSH or RDP access.
A fully managed service that extends AWS infrastructure, services, and APIs to on-premises locations, allowing customers to run AWS services locally for low-latency or data residency requirements.
A service that automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances in a fleet to match demand, maintaining performance and minimizing cost using scaling policies based on CloudWatch metrics.
A Layer 7 load balancer that distributes HTTP/HTTPS traffic across targets based on content rules such as URL paths, hostnames, and HTTP headers.
A MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible relational database engine built for the cloud that delivers up to five times the performance of MySQL with fully managed high availability and auto-scaling storage.
The lowest-cost Amazon S3 storage class, designed for data that is rarely accessed and can tolerate retrieval times of 12 to 48 hours. Suitable for long-term compliance archives.
A fully managed, scalable NFS file system for Linux workloads that automatically grows and shrinks as files are added or removed, supporting concurrent access from multiple EC2 instances across AZs.
A real-time data streaming service for ingesting, buffering, and processing large volumes of streaming data from sources like application logs, IoT devices, and clickstreams.
A serverless event bus that routes events from AWS services, custom applications, and SaaS providers to target services such as Lambda, SQS, and Step Functions based on routing rules.
A global content delivery network (CDN) with over 400 edge locations that caches content close to end users to reduce latency and improve download speeds for websites and applications.

AWS infrastructure deployments that place select services (compute, storage, database) closer to large metropolitan areas, enabling single-digit millisecond latency for latency-sensitive applications.
AWS infrastructure embedded within telecom providers' 5G networks that allows developers to build ultra-low-latency applications for mobile devices at the edge of the 5G network.
A dedicated physical network connection between an on-premises data center and AWS that bypasses the public internet, providing consistent bandwidth and lower latency.
A Storage Gateway configuration that presents a virtual tape library (VTL) interface to on-premises backup software, storing backup data as virtual tapes in S3 and archiving to S3 Glacier.
A family of physical devices (Snowcone, Snowball Edge, Snowmobile) for collecting, migrating, and processing large amounts of data in environments with limited connectivity.
A fully managed container image registry for storing, managing, and deploying Docker and OCI container images, with integrated IAM access control and vulnerability scanning.
A fully managed serverless ETL service that discovers, catalogs, and transforms data between data stores. Includes a metadata catalog (Glue Data Catalog) used by Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR.

A cloud-native business intelligence (BI) service for creating and sharing interactive dashboards and visualizations from various data sources, with ML-powered insights and a pay-per-session pricing option.
A flexible pricing model that offers up to 66–72% savings over On-Demand pricing in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of usage (measured in $/hr) for 1 or 3 years.
Spare AWS compute capacity available at up to 90% discount versus On-Demand pricing. Instances can be interrupted with 2-minute notice, making them suitable for fault-tolerant, flexible workloads.
A billing discount for EC2 (up to 72%) in exchange for a 1- or 3-year commitment to a specific instance type. Best for steady-state workloads with predictable usage.
A feature of AWS Organizations that combines the usage and billing of all member accounts into a single bill, enabling volume discounts and centralized cost management.
A service for setting up and governing a secure, multi-account AWS environment (landing zone) with pre-configured guardrails, account factory, and compliance monitoring.
IAM-like policies applied at the AWS Organizations account or OU level that set the maximum permissions available to all IAM entities in those accounts, enabling guardrails across the organization.
A service that enables sharing of AWS resources (such as VPC subnets, Transit Gateways, and Direct Connect gateways) with other AWS accounts or within an AWS Organization.
A web-based tool for estimating the cost of AWS services for planned workloads, allowing configuration of resource types, regions, and usage levels to produce a monthly cost estimate.
A service for setting custom cost and usage thresholds with automated alerts when spending approaches or exceeds the defined budget, and support for budget-driven actions.

A tool for visualizing, understanding, and analyzing AWS costs and usage over time, with filtering by service, linked account, region, and tag, plus Reserved Instance and Savings Plan recommendations.
User-defined or AWS-generated key-value tags applied to AWS resources that appear in cost reports, enabling cost visibility and chargeback by team, project, or environment.
Tiered support offerings (Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, Enterprise) providing varying levels of technical support, response times, and access to AWS experts and tooling.
A marketplace that connects AWS customers with AWS Certified experts for on-demand project help and consulting, with payment processing handled through AWS.
An AWS service that operates AWS infrastructure on behalf of customers, handling day-to-day operational activities like monitoring, patching, backup, and security for managed accounts.
A Reserved Instance type that allows changing the instance family, OS, tenancy, or payment option during the reservation term, offering flexibility at a slightly lower discount than Standard RIs.
